content:
Here is the translation of the ancient Greek text:

But then again the lord of men, Agamemnon, addressed him:
‘185 I rejoice, son of Laertes, having heard your speech.
For you have spoken and told all things in accordance with fate.
And I am willing to swear these things, and my spirit urges me,
and I will not swear falsely by a god. But let Achilles
remain there, though eager for war.
190 And let all the others remain assembled, until the gifts
come from the hut and we have sworn trusty oaths.
But to you yourself I direct this and command you:
having chosen the noblest of the Achaeans,
to bring forth from my ship the gifts which yesterday
we promised to give to Achilles, and to take women.
But let Talthybius quickly throughout the broad army of the Achaeans
prepare a boar, to sacrifice to Zeus and Helios.
